title: Consistent brand cues and reach-first media on small budgets
origin: ClimbOS synthesis (original proposal) from the member frameworks; author guidance is cited by finding id, proposed rules are labelled 'proposed'.
decision_task: How to keep brand cues consistent and early in content and ads, and when to favour reach and continuity over narrow targeting.
applies_when: Recurring consumer or local business with ongoing content or ads
exclusions: Small niche B2B where reach has a low ceiling
evidence_requirements: Inventory of every asset in current collateral (site, socials, listings, van or shopfront, packaging, ads)
Optional: masked-asset survey of category buyers (asset shown without the name; 'which business or brand is this?' open answer)
Platform-reported unique reach and frequency for the service area
Where the business can actually deliver or sell
Share of annual sales in peak season
whether buyers search shortly before buying (recency category)
opening hours, ordering routes, delivery coverage
missing_data_behavior: No brand kit: skip asset checks; name the business early.

decision_branches.then: Vary the angle, keep identity cues.

implementation_steps: Lay out all collateral together and list what repeats and what clashes (table test)
Choose a varied palette, starting with one or two items usable on pack/storefront and at the start of videos
Pair each asset with the name prominently in every execution
Check legibility at thumbnail size for online listings and feeds
For variants or new services: parent assets first, then a variant twist
Optionally survey fame and uniqueness; compute in code; place on the grid
Define category buyers in the area and the period
Compute the response rate needed for the sales target at each reach level (in code)
Buy reach: broad targeting within the area, frequency watched, continuous presence
Audit physical availability (hours, locations, apps, stockists, booking friction)
dependencies: A brand kit or the minimal provisional kit already defined by instagram-posts and social-visual-briefs
For metrics: category-buyer respondents, not just followers
Physical availability in the targeted area (K6)

cash_and_labor_requirements.cash: Zero for the audit; survey cost unknown
cash_and_labor_requirements.capability: Design consistency across tools; brand kit in ClimbOS

metrics: Fame = respondents naming the brand for the asset / all respondents
Uniqueness = mentions of the brand for the asset / all brand mentions for the asset
Share of published pieces carrying the declared assets in the first frame or slide (ClimbOS proxy)
Unique reach in the service area
Sales or inquiries per period versus baseline
guardrails: Fame x uniqueness audit needs a survey of category buyers; customer-only surveys are biased.
Required-response arithmetic is done in code.
Don't derive assets from the current positioning claim
Don't copy a competitor's assets (trademark and trade-dress risk)
Don't change logo, packaging or colours for 'freshness'
Don't plan for a minimum frequency of 3
Don't trade reach for 'engagement' formats without comparing the cost per category buyer reached
Spend only within approved caps; external actions need owner approval
Respect special ad category and geographic targeting rules
Even monthly spend preferred to bursts unless a seasonal peak is real
No paid reach without owner budget approval
Never treat impressions as people reached
alternatives_when_constrained: No survey budget: consistency audit plus an informal masked check with a few locals, labelled anecdotal
No budget: owned reach (storefront, van, packaging, Google Business Profile, partners' audiences, flyers)
No reach data: use the platform's reach estimate, labelled as an estimate
No ad budget: physical availability fixes, local listings, partner placements, consistent organic posting
No tracking: self-reported 'how did you hear' at checkout
stop_conditions: Re-test yearly or after a major campaign; if uniqueness falls because a competitor copies the asset, pair it more strongly with the name
Weekly: frequency versus reach. Quarterly: sales versus baseline. Stop a channel if its reach is mostly duplicated.
Reach channel: review at 3 months on new-buyer trend and branded search, not 8-week inquiries
review_triggers: Owner's numbers or business type change
A dated benchmark this playbook mentions is superseded
Category-generic colours (e.g. blue in dental): execute them in a distinctive way, like the book's HSBC red border example
Platform minimum spends and learning phases that make very small budgets inefficient
Regulated categories with targeting limits (special ad categories)
Small budgets spread so thin that no one sees the ad more than once a quarter
Platform 'reach' that isn't attention (FAQ: social OTS vs actual brains)

strategic_preference.rule: proposed: Every set of posts or ads carries the same one or two declared brand assets in the first frame or slide, while angles and buying situations vary.
proposed: Prefer continuous lower-weight presence to a single burst unless sales are highly seasonal.
proposed rule: a physical-availability check (hours, ordering routes, stockists, booking friction) runs before any awareness spend for consumer businesses

contextual_heuristic.rule: proposed: Video ads and scripts make the business identifiable early, through the product or owner carrying a declared asset in frame 1 or the name on screen within the opening, and again later. A hook-first opening is fine if branding comes within it.
proposed: Don't recommend a logo, packaging or colour change without a recorded reason (legal, merger, asset fails a test) and a re-education plan.

proposed: Paid social drafts for consumer and local businesses default to broad targeting within the service area, not narrow interest or persona targeting, unless eligibility, capacity or a listable B2B target set requires narrowing.
proposed: A second platform needs a stated reason it reaches different people; two similar social platforms on a small budget are flagged.

proposed rule: use the frequency dimension in scoring: for recurring B2C, soften the intent penalty on broad-reach families (paid_social, video, local, traditional) by a bounded amount when the budget band supports them
proposed rule: paid reach plans spread spend evenly by month unless the owner names a seasonal peak
proposed rule: reach-channel stop rules use a 3-month window and new-buyer trend, not 8-week inquiries

external_requirement.rule: proposed: Never imitate a competitor's distinctive assets.

missing_prerequisite.rule: proposed: Fame and uniqueness are computed in code with n shown.
proposed: When an owner proposes a low-reach tactic, show the required response rate (target / (category buyers x reach)) computed in code.
proposed: Ad geography must match where the business can deliver.

unknown_to_investigate.rule: proposed rule: whether reach channels beat demand capture for small recurring-B2C budgets is unknown; run a geo holdout when budget allows

reconciliation_note: Revises the 'never open with the brand name' rule (RECONCILIATION R07).
